clue.text: Excited at a cheap bill with a certain order

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to find a bargain bill arranged just so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' looks like it describes a person, but it tells you to rearrange AT A CHEAP BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arranged A to Z follow a particular fixed sequence, the order of the letters.

clue.text: It could be the thing

definitions.meaning: an item or object, as in 'an ... of clothing'

explanation.surface: A vague remark that something might be the very item wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, and an item or object is also called an article.

clue.text: Parking up with pastries for little nippers?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
taken as written
pies are baked pastry dishes

explanation.surface: Someone parks and heads up the road with a bag of pastries for the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little nippers' usually means small children; here it is young dogs that nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Young dogs are small creatures that like to nip, a playful take on a slang word for children.

clue.text: Creatures great and small grabbing first aid offered by this person?

indicators.note: the two creatures grab or hold between them the letters for the ordinal, so these go inside

parts.note: a donkey is the larger of the two creatures
an ant is the small creature
1ST, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An echo of the hymn 'All things bright and beautiful, all creatures great and small', with first aid thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' means the two creatures hold the ordinal between them; the figure 1 in '1st' is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide is a person whose job is giving help to someone else.

clue.text: Shove the Spanish child's dog, half-cut

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, leaving the first half

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog

explanation.surface: A tipsy pushing match over a Spanish child's pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like slang for drunk, but it tells you to take off half of BOWWOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To push someone aside with the arm is a synonym used as a verb: to nudge or jostle.

clue.text: Picture of island men following star once viewed regularly

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men who followed the star to Bethlehem

indicators.note: looking at every other letter of the word once picks out its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A painting of island folk trailing a star that was seen long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewed regularly' picks the alternate letters N and E from 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, a straightforward synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Make of liquid I've taken in pain

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are taken inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed form, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of liquid someone has swallowed while in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges I'VE to IEV, which is 'taken in' by ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make the grade or make it is to succeed, to accomplish a goal.

clue.text: Sisters' place with a lino designed to be boring?

parts.note: a convent is where nuns, called sisters, live

indicators.note: designed means arranged into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nunnery fitted with plain lino flooring that is deliberately dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges A LINO to IONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unadventurous and traditional can seem dull, so the question mark flags a loose fit.

clue.text: One having many members in work after month

indicators.note: the work comes after the month in the answer

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A club with a large membership that started operating after a particular month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests a club, but it means limbs: eight arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea creature has eight arms, and limbs are also called members.

clue.text: British trains losing time in seaside places

indicators.note: the word for trains loses a letter

parts.note: to train is to teach

explanation.surface: British railway trains running late in holiday resorts by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like railway carriages, but it is the verb meaning instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy shores are the places at the seaside where people sunbathe.

clue.text: This person entering exams works OK

indicators.note: the setter's I goes into the word for exams

parts.note: SATS are national school tests in Britain
the setter referring to themself as I
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A candidate sitting exams finds the paper fine.
explanation.walkthrough: SATS are standard assessment tests taken by schoolchildren in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable or adequate is up to the required standard, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Two men, both short and small, used as fall guys

parts.note: Vic and Tim are short forms of Victor and Timothy

explanation.surface: A pair of short men and a little one are set up to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' means shortened names, not short stature: VIC and TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapegoats who take the blame or get duped are those who suffer at others' hands.

clue.text: Top Ten record maybe covered by One Direction, extremely colourless

indicators.note: the record goes inside, enclosed by the direction

parts.note: west is one compass direction
a hit is a chart-topping record

explanation.surface: A boy band covering a chart hit in a very bland version.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a boy band, but here it is simply a compass point, WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a pale shade: most lacking in colour, as pale as can be.

clue.text: Pines for Eden dug up with spades

indicators.note: soil dug up is turned over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A gardener longing for paradise turns over the soil with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug up' rearranges EDEN to NEED. 'Pines' looks like trees but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for or yearn after something is to want it badly.

clue.text: A peculiar raw sense in knowing what's going on

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd, unrefined instinct that helps someone read a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert to and conscious of one's surroundings is a state of knowledge.

clue.text: Put delivery label on dead fashionable netting skirt

indicators.note: the shuffled letters net or catch the garment inside them
fashionable read as fashioned anew, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: a dress is a skirted garment

explanation.surface: A fashion item described as dead trendy, with a netted skirt, is labelled for posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges DEAD to ADED, which is 'netting' DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing the name and destination on a parcel prepares it for posting.

clue.text: Examined bug placed by journalist receiving pressure

indicators.note: the journalist is placed beside the bug
the bug receives the pressure letter inside it

parts.note: an insect is a bug
P is the symbol for pressure
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A bug is planted by a reporter under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like a listening device but is an insect; 'receiving' puts P inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Looked at closely or scrutinised is the past tense sense matching the clue's verb.

clue.text: Cult number one upwardly-mobile area

parts.note: a sect is a religious group or cult

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cult's leading member rises in status in the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly-mobile' turns NO plus I around to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A part or zone of something, such as a district or a portion, is a synonym.

clue.text: Carry off pretty trailing flower in Devon

indicators.note: the word for pretty trails behind the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon; a flower is something that flows
cute means pretty

explanation.surface: Someone takes away a lovely flower hanging over in a Devon garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, a river: the Exe, which runs through the English county of Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out or perform a task, or to pull it off successfully, is a synonym.

clue.text: Player that makes more

definitions.meaning: a film walk-on actor with no lines
something additional, adding to the total

explanation.surface: A performer who increases the total.
explanation.definitionFit: A film walk-on is a background actor, and something additional is a bonus on top.

clue.text: Someone dining given seconds by new Chinese, perhaps

indicators.note: the diner is given the letter inside

parts.note: an eater is someone eating a meal

explanation.surface: A diner offered second helpings at a new Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese' looks like a takeaway meal, but is an example of something from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese culture is an example of something Oriental, from Asia.

clue.text: Part of hospital where tragedies may be played out

definitions.meaning: an operating room where surgery is done

definitions.text: where tragedies may be played out
definitions.meaning: a playhouse where tragic plays are staged

explanation.surface: A grim reflection that sad events unfold on hospital wards.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating room in a hospital shares its name with a playhouse for drama.

clue.text: Core group of students to welcome around the French university

indicators.note: the union welcomes the other letters inside it

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
C, short for circa, means around
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A core of students welcomes visitors around a French university.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student body.
explanation.definitionFit: The central part or heart of something, like an atom's centre, is a synonym.

clue.text: Rude to axe old boy that's part of act

indicators.note: the letters for old boy are axed or cut from the word

parts.note: obscene means rude or indecent
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Cutting a crude old man from part of a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's act is divided into smaller units, each a segment of the drama.

clue.text: Energy goes before a nap that's cut short — most convenient!

indicators.note: the energy letter comes first

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: Energy levels rise before an interrupted nap: the handiest arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Least difficult or simplest to do is the superlative meaning handiest.

clue.text: Left back that is certain to get time off

indicators.note: back means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A footballer playing left back is sure of a break from training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' looks like a football position, but 'back' reverses the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Free hours spent away from work are relaxation time.

clue.text: Southern climate — husband's taken off warm clothing

indicators.note: the husband letter is removed from the word

parts.note: weather is loosely the climate

explanation.surface: In a hot southern climate the husband strips off his woollens.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is a garment worn for warmth.

clue.text: Standing alone in deep end moving a bit, pleasant but I must get out

indicators.note: the letters move around a bit, so they are rearranged
the I must get out of the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A swimmer stuck in the deep end edges around, pleasant but desperate to climb out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving a bit' rearranges IN DEEP END to INDEPENDE; NICE without I gives NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reliance, standing on one's own feet without outside support, is the noun's sense.
